messages:
maya_g: Quick sync — we need a single observability surface for error modes: timeouts, 5xx, OOMs, and degraded-mode/fallback counts. Goal: product + oncall can quickly see root cause by route/model/region.

alex.k: +1. I can draft the dashboard. Need raw metric names from runtime/route layer. Propose tags: model, route, region, capacity_tier, fallback_type.

tj: Also include routing-policy label (e.g. primary|fallback|canary) — some 5xx spikes are actually fallback traffic.

maya_g: Good call on routing-policy. Priya: from Console POV, we want per-route links from panel -> route rollout history + recent quota events. Can we attach route_id to metrics?

priya: Yes — route_id is already emitted by the API-gateway for auth/quotas, but runtime metrics currently use route_name. We should standardize to route_id for joins. UX: one click to open rollout timeline and last 5 quota hits.

samira: Technically, we emit these from two places: runtime agents (latency/status/oom_count) and the routing proxy (quota/retry/fallback_trigger). We'll add a consistent label `route_id`. Need owners to add the label across both pipelines.

alex.k: For panel design: counters for `requests_total{status=5xx}`, `timeouts_total`, `oom_count`, and `fallbacks_total` split by `fallback_type`. Also a rate per-minute and a 1h rolling count. Use heatmap by region.

maya_g: For degraded-mode, we should count both automatic degraded responses (e.g., Abbrev fallback) and manual circuit-breaker activations. Can we add `degraded_mode=auto|manual`?

samira: Yep. We'll emit `degraded_mode` label from the orchestration layer. Note: high cardinality risk if we also tag with `node_id`. Keep node details for investigation panels only.

priya: UX note: make panels cross-filterable by model and by deployment tag (hosted/dedicated/private). Customers care about private infra OOMs.

alex.k: Agreed. I'll include a top row of KPIs: overall error rate, p99 latency, fallback rate, oom rate. Below: time-series and a table of recent spikes with suggested likely cause (based on heuristics).

tj: Heuristics example: if 5xx spike + increased fallback_rate -> likely model crash or resource saturation on runtime; if timeouts spike without 5xx -> network/queue. We should codify these into alert runbooks.

maya_g: Alerts: want two SLO-based alerts (error-rate and latency) and one operational alert for sudden fallback surge (>=200% baseline in 5m). Who will own alert thresholds? ops-oncall?

samira: We'll own infra-level alerts. Platform/console owns application-facing SLO alerts. We'll share a draft with threshold suggestions.

priya: For rollouts UX integration: can we link a panel row to the rollout id and show the active policy? If fallback surge correlates with a canary, allow quick rollback link.

alex.k: From telemetry side, we need these metric name conventions: `redwood.requests.count`, `redwood.requests.latency_ms`, `redwood.requests.ooms`, `redwood.requests.fallbacks`. Labels: `route_id`, `model`, `region`, `routing_policy`, `degraded_mode`, `fallback_type`. I'll open a PR in dashboards repo with JSON panels and a README.

maya_g: Timeline: get labels instrumented by EOD Tuesday, dashboards draft Wed, share to owners Thu for feedback. Ops to test alerts Fri. Is that feasible? :calendar:

samira: EOD Tue for labels is tight but doable if we limit to route_id + degraded_mode + fallback_type first. We'll follow up with a short changelist.

priya: I'll sketch the Console links by Wed.

alex.k: I'll add a small query example in the PR: ```sum(rate(redwood.requests.fallbacks[5m])) by (route_id, fallback_type)``` and a panel that shows fallback proportion vs total requests.

ops-bot: Alert created: Fallback surge watch (owner: eng-sre) — draft rule saved, not firing.

deploy-bot: Deployed: routing-proxy#release-2026.03.18 — added route_id to emitted events in staging.

maya_g: Awesome — thanks team. Follow-ups: alex.k will open PR, samira confirm label rollout plan, priya wire the Console link mock, tj coordinate runbook entries. We'll sync next week if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
